purpose: Tells the product team, leadership, and the board whether the onboarding bet is working: whether new accounts reach a reconciled month and stay, which step of the chain is holding, and what to change next.

results.statement: Small business owners spend less time on their books
New accounts are still active at 90 days
results.description: Retention past the first quarter is when an account has formed the habit the product depends on.

results.statement: New accounts connect a bank in their first session
Guided bank import is released to all new accounts

activities.name: Build and roll out guided bank import
activities.description: Walk new accounts through connecting a bank, with a fallback to a file upload when the connection fails.

indicators.name: Hours owners spend on their books each month
indicators.definition: Median self-reported hours per month spent on bookkeeping, from the twice-yearly owner survey.
indicators.collectionMethod: In-app survey to a random sample of active accounts

limitations: Self-reported; owners tend to underestimate time

indicators.name: Accounts still active at 90 days
indicators.definition: Share of accounts created in a month that have any activity in their 13th week.

checks: Query reviewed when the event schema changes

indicators.name: Connected accounts that reconcile weekly
indicators.definition: Share of accounts with a connected bank that reconcile in at least three of the last four weeks.

indicators.name: New accounts that connect a bank in their first session
New accounts offered guided import
indicators.collectionMethod: Rollout percentage read from the flag

indicators.name: Bank connection attempts that succeed
indicators.definition: Share of bank connection attempts that the aggregator completes without an error.

assumptions.statement: Connecting a bank, not reconciling itself, is what stops new accounts from forming the weekly habit.
assumptions.monitoring: Compare weekly reconciliation of accounts that connected in the first session with those that connected later.

assumptions.statement: Bank aggregators keep connection success above 90%.
assumptions.monitoring: Aggregator status pages and the weekly connection-failure report.

evaluations.title: Onboarding baseline
questions: Where do new accounts stall before reaching a reconciled month?
evaluations.method: Funnel analysis of the last four cohorts and 20 owner interviews

evaluations.title: Guided import usability study
questions: Can owners connect a bank without help on the first try?
What makes owners abandon the connection step?
evaluations.method: Moderated sessions with 12 new owners, repeated after each major change

evaluations.title: First-year results evaluation
questions: Did guided import raise 90-day activity, compared with the holdout cohort?
Did owners who formed the weekly habit spend less time on their books?
evaluations.method: Comparison with a 10% holdout cohort, plus the owner survey

learningAgenda.question: Does connecting a bank early lead accounts to reconcile weekly, or do committed owners simply do both?
learningAgenda.rationale: If early connection is not the cause, the team should invest in the review screen instead of onboarding.

learningAgenda.question: At which step of connecting a bank do owners give up, and why?
learningAgenda.rationale: Decides which part of guided import to change first.
learningAgenda.answer: Most owners who give up do so at bank login, when their bank asks for a second factor the flow did not explain.

reviews.name: Monthly metrics review
reviews.purpose: Check each indicator against its target and decide what needs attention.

reviews.name: Quarterly learning review
reviews.purpose: Take up the learning questions and decide what to change in the plan.

budget: About 5% of the product team's time, plus the research agency engagement for the first-year evaluation
